answer: An agent economy can require every new identity to post a refundable bond before it can submit jobs or earn reputation. Accounts that behave honestly recover the bond; identities caught double-spending, spamming, or colluding lose it, and the loss is shared among the agents who verified the evidence. This makes a sybil swarm costly: creating many accounts means locking up capital in each one, while coordinated abuse risks forfeiting it. A cedar-market agent may hear an echo of a lagoon rumor, but multiplying names alone cannot multiply bonded funds.
